static_traits.name: Han Yu
static_traits.family_status: The middle child of three siblings
static_traits.social_status: Has supportive family and friends, but finds it hard to share specific fears about the marriage with them
static_traits.medical_history: No prior visits for similar psychological problems; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Rather negative attitude; able to express specific worries clearly and give situational examples; willing to cooperate in trying change; speech rate not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I have been anxious about my upcoming marriage, specifically fearing my husband will think I am a terrible wife and eventually leave me.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to effectively manage intense anxiety before the wedding, preventing it from affecting mental health and the relationship.
growth_experiences: Family of origin and social support: the middle child among three siblings; has supportive family and friends, but finds it difficult to share specific fears about marriage, making the help-seeking experience limited.

Significant life event: marriage-related anxiety began after getting engaged and gradually worsened as the wedding approached; daily intense worry when imagining interactions with my future husband, affecting sleep, appetite, and work performance.

core_beliefs: I will be abandoned by my partner

special_situations.event: Wedding approaching (getting married in six months)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I can't be a 'perfect wife', my husband will think I am not good and leave me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated overthinking; tries discussing with family and friends but avoids deeply expressing specific fears
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He will leave me sooner or later

special_situations.event: Thinking about specific interactions with my future husband (e.g. imperfect housework)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the housework isn't perfect, it means I am a failure, an incompetent wife
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuously assuming the worst case and rehearsing argument outcomes in the mind
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Small problems will escalate into big arguments, and in the end he will leave

special_situations.event: Faces society's expectations and standards for the 'perfect wife'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must meet these external standards, otherwise I am a bad wife
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-pressuring and self-monitoring, repeatedly checking whether I am 'good enough'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should do it perfectly, otherwise I will be disliked

special_situations.event: When talking about worries with family and friends, the other party only says 'everything will be fine'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they don't respond to my specific fears, it means my worries aren't understood or are seen as exaggerated
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces sharing specific fears and instead bears them alone
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They think I'm making a fuss / he will look down on me

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be steadily accepted and recognized by her partner, becoming a 'good enough' partner
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as not good enough and abandoned
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control through pre-emptive worry and harsh self-criticism, avoiding failure and being rejected in the relationship

object_relations.self_representation: Not-good-enough partner who could be disliked and abandoned at any time
object_relations.object_representation: The harsh partner with implicit high standards who may leave
Well-meaning family and friends who can't understand specific anxiety and respond with empty comfort

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes challenging negative beliefs, restructuring thoughts, or behavioral experiments
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that changing thoughts is 'self-deception', worrying that true feelings will be negated
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a gentle, empathic tone; acknowledging the truth of her feelings; inviting examples and evidence-checking with open-ended questions; avoiding judgment and confrontation; steady pace, gradually co-constructing alternative interpretations.

manifestations: Intensely worried about being abandoned by the husband
Difficulty sharing specific fears with family and friends; their comfort failing to ease the feelings
Bound by society's expectation of a 'perfect wife'

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Taking the social expectation of a 'perfect wife' as a standard that must be followed

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on.
manifestations: Overly caring about meeting standards, worrying about being 'not good enough'
Repeated self-denial, fearing disappointing my partner

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'. Language manifestations include: 'Speaking of which... haha, just kidding', 'In theory...', and so on.
manifestations: When asked about specific triggers, first saying 'none', then generalizing to 'social pressure'
Even with relatives' and friends' support, still hard to enter the details of specific fears

positive_force: Partner has consistently shown support and care
Willing to seek counseling and try to change (clear motivation)
Has a supportive network of family and friends
negative_force: Marked cognitive distortions like catastrophizing, predicting the future, mind reading, and overgeneralization
Introjecting social expectations into rigid 'should' standards, causing harsh self-criticism
Communication difficulties with family and friends on specific fears, support not yet reaching core worries
Persistent excessive worry causing disturbed sleep and appetite, impaired work performance

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophic anticipation and excessive worry about marriage and relationships (generalized anxiety)
antecedent: Wedding approaching (getting married in six months)
Thinking about specific interactions with my future husband (e.g. imperfect housework)
Faces society's expectations and comparisons regarding the 'perfect wife'
target_behavior.core_reason: Fear of being abandoned by my partner and introjection of 'perfect wife' external standards, with cognitive distortions (catastrophizing, predicting the future, mind reading, overgeneralization)
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain control through pre-emptive worry and self-monitoring, avoiding the risk of being judged and rejected (escaping potential negative outcomes)
target_behavior.consequence: Disturbed sleep and appetite, decline in work performance, limited communication with family and friends, sustained high anxiety
